item.title: Deobfuscating Local Auto-Login Wallets in Oracle 26ai
item.description:
The previous post explained how to deobfuscate auto-login wallets in Oracle 26ai and recover the contents of the ewallet.p12 file from a cwallet.sso file (see also 1). This post now takes a closer look at how Oracle 26ai obfuscates local auto-login wallets and what has changed compared with earlier releases.

The Oracle 26ai Security Guide states that local auto-login wallets have been made more secure (see also 2), but provides no details on what this additional security consists of:

item.title: Deobfuscating Auto-Login Wallets in Oracle 26ai
item.description:
After looking into how Oracle obfuscates credential passwords and database link passwords in version 26ai (see also 1 and 2), I started wondering how auto-login wallets are obfuscated and whether the obfuscation has changed in 26ai as well.

Prior public research on that topic dates back to Oracle 11g (see also 3, 4, and 5), and I couldn’t find any information related to 26ai, so I decided to have a look myself.
